# Legacy factory compatibility (Rust migration)

Scenario v2 does not use factories. Author new integrations with `define_scenario` or `define_scenario_up_only` and ordinary code inside `up`/`down`, as described in `implement.md` and `scenarios.md`.

This page exists only for projects migrating older customer code that already calls `define_factory`. The helper is not registered with the handler, is not discoverable, and is never invoked by the v2 protocol. Do not introduce it in a new v2 integration.

## Temporary use during migration

Existing helper calls may remain temporarily while their creation and cleanup behavior moves into scenario-owned functions. New v2 code should call those functions directly from `up` and `down`.

## The shape

`define_factory(input_fields, create, teardown, ref_fields)` returns a `FactoryDefinition`. The convenience wrapper `define_factory_create_only(input_fields, create)` omits teardown and ref fields.

```rust
use autonoma_sdk::factory::define_factory;
use autonoma_sdk::types::{FactoryContext, FieldDef};
use serde_json::{Map, Value};

let user_factory = define_factory(
    vec![
        FieldDef { name: "email".into(), field_type: "string".into(), required: true },
        FieldDef { name: "orgId".into(), field_type: "string".into(), required: true },
    ],
    |data: &Map<String, Value>, _ctx: &FactoryContext| Box::pin(async move {
        // ... your real creation code ...
        let mut record = Map::new();
        record.insert("id".into(), Value::String("user_123".into()));
        record.insert("email".into(), data.get("email").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null));
        Ok(record)
    }),
    Some(|record: &Map<String, Value>, _ctx: &FactoryContext| Box::pin(async move {
        let _id = record.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str());
        // ... your real delete code ...
        Ok(())
    })),
    None,
);
```

- `input_fields: Vec<FieldDef>` describes the create payload. `FieldDef` is `{ name, field_type, required }`; `field_type` is an SDK type string (`"string"`, `"integer"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`, `"timestamp"`, `"date"`, `"uuid"`, `"json"`). `validate_input` checks a `Map` against these before you call `create`.
- `create(data, ctx)` runs your real creation code and returns a `serde_json::Map<String, Value>` that includes at least an `"id"` key.
- `teardown(record, ctx)` optionally deletes the record. Pass `None` (or use `define_factory_create_only`) and the factory creates but does not delete.
- `ref_fields: Option<Vec<FieldDef>>` optionally describes the shape of the stored record.

`ctx` is a `FactoryContext`: `{ refs: HashMap<String, Vec<Map<String, Value>>>, scenario_name: String, test_run_id: String }`. Factories that need a database connection get it from the host (their own pool/ORM); the SDK provides only `refs` and `test_run_id`.

## Using a factory from a scenario

A factory is a plain value whose `create_fn`/`teardown_fn` you call yourself; wire its output into your scenario's `teardown` so `down` can undo it. Because it is not wired to the protocol, you drive it by hand - there is no registry the handler reads. For most scenarios, skip it: plain code in `up`/`down` is the default.
